description: We are a passionate team gearing up for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our focus is to solve the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge by creating an immersive, interactive, and gamified web application (E-learning Platform) that inspires the next generation of space explorers.
summary:
We developed an educational strategic game for children aged between 7-12 that help them at planning a mission on both Moon and Mars. The game delivers the space science by translating the abstract posters and advanced engineering simulators, letting kids directly experience the real trade-offs astronauts and mission planners.
Players command a lunar mission or a martian one and play through a 14-day interactive adventure.
managing a tight resource economy where every unit of power there must be physically allocated between life support, radiation shielding, science labs, and food production.
It is very important because it grounds children's play in genuine space missions, planetary science and live NASA data (such as solar flares from the DONKI API) without making it hard for them.
And at the conclusion: teaching them that no choice in space is free and that every decision carries a compounded consequence.

details:
What it does & How it works: Outpost Director immerses the player in a 6-stage daily mission loop over a 14-day/Sol mission on either the Lunar South Pole or Jezero Crater on Mars. Guided by an AI copilot named A.S.T.R.O., players face daily space-weather events and decision cards with risk tiers (safe, balanced, risky). The core mechanic is a drag-and-drop energy allocator where players distribute a limited pool of power cubes.
Benefits & Goals: The primary goal is teaching trade-off thinking and system resilience. Visual feedback (such as screens fogging blue when oxygen drops or lights dimming during power scarcity) makes abstract numbers feel real. It features non-punitive failure handling, full accessibility (ARIA, keyboard navigation), and awards up to 7 distinct merit badges based on play style.

Tech Stack & Tools: Built using Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript 5, and Tailwind CSS v4. The architecture relies on a pure simulation core (engine.ts) with zero external state libraries (useReducer), a custom SVG scene engine (BaseScene.tsx), and a Web Audio API synthesizer for sound effects without heavy asset downloads.
